Predict the human participant's submitted initial transfer in a Trust Game. You are making role A's choice with an anonymous other Amazon Mechanical Turk worker as partner B. You start with 40 US cents ($0.40), and choose how much a to send to B, from zero up to all 40 cents. You keep 40-a cents before any return. The experiment triples your transfer: B receives 3a cents and may return any amount r from that received pot, from zero up to 3a. A return is voluntary and is not guaranteed. Under an implemented pair of decisions, A ends with 40-a+r cents; B keeps 3a-r cents from the received pot. You cannot change B's later return. Giving 0 sends nothing, and giving 40 sends the entire initial endowment. These are descriptions of the rules, not recommended choices.
Every participant first submits an A-role transfer and later completes B-role return decisions for hypothetical transfers. The B decisions are contingencies, not observed transfers from an actual partner, and do not mean several simultaneous payouts. Participants are told that one role will be selected at random to determine their bonus; no probability for the role draw is specified here. No actual selected role, partner's submitted choice, matching result, return or payment has been revealed at this first A decision. The fixed participation payment is 30 US cents ($0.30), separate from the game. The instructions announce the opportunity to earn up to $1.20 in additional bonuses depending on both people's decisions. Do not infer the partner's character or generosity, or replace a submitted transfer with an assumed paid bonus.
All amounts in the current query and answer are US cents: 100 cents equals one US dollar. Predict the amount actually sent, not the amount kept, the tripled sum, a later return or a percentage. Use integer cents from 0 through 40, preserving the recorded monetary precision. This is the first monetary decision of this game. Factual background belongs to you, not to B; an empty object means no reliable individual fact is supplied. Where earlier questionnaire answers are provided, they are this person's actual prior reports, not objective personality facts or known reports about B. Return only the integer US-cent transfer from 0 through 40, without units or explanation.

The six-item questionnaire comes after this game; its answers have not yet been collected at this decision.

Before this game you completed a six-item questionnaire. The item descriptions in order are: (1) having much in life to be thankful for; (2) expecting a very long list of things one is grateful for; (3) seeing little to be grateful for in the world; (4) being grateful to a wide variety of people; (5) becoming more able with age to appreciate people, events and situations in one's life; (6) going long periods without feeling grateful to someone or something. The six raw answers below are in this item order, including the negatively worded items 3 and 6 without reversing them. They describe completed self-reports; do not turn them into a personality diagnosis or an assumed feeling about the current partner. No calculated score or score feedback is supplied.
